items.title: Efficient and precise programmable DNA knock-in without double-strand breaks
items.summary: Kilobase-scale nickase-targeting (KNIT) editing enables single-nick-based DNA insertion across genomic loci and cell types, supporting insertion of DNA fragments exceeding 10 kb, with high efficiency and minimal unwanted off-target effects.

items.title: Precise DNA base editing using AlphaFold3-based contact modelling
items.summary: ContactSeek is an AlphaFold3-driven model that can improve the precision of genome-editing tools.

items.title: Bizarre CRISPR enzyme kills cancer cells by shredding their DNA
items.summary: Early tests suggest the protein can be aimed at targets with tumour-causing mutations.

items.title: AI identifies interactions in CRISPR complexes to improve specificity of DNA editing
items.summary: AlphaFold3 predictions of the molecular contacts made by a genome-editing enzyme have been used to improve the enzyme’s selectivity for target DNA sequences.

items.title: Planetary-mass exosatellite detected around the substellar companion of a star
items.summary: Radial velocity measurements provide evidence for a Jupiter-mass exosatellite orbiting the brown dwarf companion CD-35 2722 B, a promising detection of an exomoon-like object.

items.title: Personalized gene therapy relieves severe epilepsy in two boys
items.summary: Switching off one copy of a gene also enabled one of the children to walk independently for the first time.

items.title: Structures and inhibition of the Crimean–Congo haemorrhagic fever virus polymerase
items.summary: Structural studies of Crimean–Congo haemorrhagic fever virus (CCHFV) polymerase reveal the structural basis of CCHFV RNA synthesis and highlight druggable sites for designing both nucleoside antivirals and non-nucleoside antivirals.

items.title: AI-redesigned starting points and outcomes enhance protein evolution
items.summary: A workflow using artificial intelligence-redesigned starting points to evolve enzymes with improved properties compared with those evolved from natural proteins is established.

items.title: Fly neurons carry a molecular ‘timestamp’ that encodes their birth order
items.summary: A single-cell gene-expression atlas of the fly nerve cord mapped onto its wiring diagram has uncovered a simple shared gene-expression code. The code enables neurons to carry a molecular memory of the order of their birth from a parent cell, and shapes their diversity.

items.title: This El Niño is set to be the largest on record by a ‘mind-blowing margin’
items.summary: Forecasters predict that the monster climate pattern will combine with global warming to push global temperatures in 2027 to new heights.

items.title: CRISPR–Cas regulates expression of embedded anti-phage defence systems
items.summary: CRISPR–Cas systems transcriptionally tune diverse innate defences using CRISPR RNA-like guides to balance antiviral protection with fitness, and hyperactivate these defences when compromised, establishing a layered bacterial ‘immunity guard’ network.

items.title: A global molecular code for birth order and neuronal identity in Drosophila
items.summary: A high-resolution developmental transcriptional atlas of the Drosophila melanogaster nerve cord identifies a shared transcriptional code that records neuronal birth order and organizes neuronal diversity.

items.title: Genetic background sets the trajectory of experimental cancer evolution
items.summary: Experimentally replaying tumour evolution in divergent mouse strains reveals the importance of interactions between genetic ancestry and acquired cancer-driving mutations in shaping the earliest stages of cancer development.

items.title: Electronic-resonance enhanced molecule for perovskite solar cells
items.summary: Electronic-resonance enhanced molecule for perovskite solar cells

items.title: Prior therapy defines mutation profiles in childhood cancer at relapse
items.summary: Chemotherapy, particularly with platinum-based drugs, is associated with substantial, rapidly detectable mutagenesis in childhood cancers, tripling private signatures and doubling mutation burden, highlighting therapy-induced tumour evolution and opportunities for safer, de-escalated treatment.

items.title: Tertiary lymphoid structures harbour stem-like tumour-specific T cells
items.summary: Renal cell carcinoma tumours containing tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs) are enriched for exhausted CD8+ T cells, including tumour-specific clonotypes with stem-like progenitor features and reduced terminal exhaustion.

items.title: Background genetics and new mutations interact to direct cancer evolution
items.summary: Rerunning tumour evolution in mice shows how cancer develops after DNA damage and reveals that background genetics and acquired mutations interact to shape genome stability and selection. This provides experimental evidence that genetic ancestry has an important role in setting the trajectory of cancer evolution.

items.title: Non-epitaxial perovskite polariton laser diode operating under direct current
items.summary: By integrating a solution-grown perovskite microplate with chemically inert single-walled carbon nanotube electrodes and embedding them into an optical microcavity, the new microdevices can achieve polariton lasing under a constant direct current at 8 K.

items.title: RNA synthesis and substrate analog inhibition in the CCHFV polymerase
items.summary: RNA synthesis and substrate analog inhibition in the CCHFV polymerase

items.title: A vector-based strategy for olfactory navigation in Drosophila
items.summary: Using a virtual reality system, experiments in Drosophila show that flies use memory mechanisms to navigate along the boundary of an odour plume and track the source of a smell.

items.title: Non-Gaussian statistics of the order parameter across a phase transition
items.summary: Single-atom measurements show non-Gaussian order-parameter fluctuations and critical scaling across a continuous phase transition, highlighting the importance of full statistical distributions in understanding universality.

items.title: Structural basis of the RNA-editing cascade in trypanosome mitochondria
items.summary: Cryo-electron microscopy sheds light on the architecture of the Trypanosoma brucei mitochondrial editosome and reveals how this assembly mediates mRNA editing through the insertion and deletion of uridine nucleotides.

items.title: Insulator-free topological photonic multi-lane highways
items.summary: An insulator-free topological waveguide architecture comprising four inequivalent photonic valley half-semimetals arranged in a parallel, cyclic configuration and stacked very close to one another demonstrates robust, multi-lane, unidirectional light transport with 100% spatial efficiency.

items.title: Semiconducting and magnetic lanthanide MXenes from intercalated halides
items.summary: A bottom-up synthesis strategy creates lanthanide MXenes (Ln2CT2) that combine semiconducting behaviour with ferromagnetism, offering a promising new class of two-dimensional materials for spintronic applications.

items.title: Subnuclear genome compartmentalization controls bivalent chromatin activity
items.summary: Knowledge of the spatial location of a gene is necessary to understand its epigenomic regulation.

items.title: Imaging of nanoscale polar textures in quantum paraelectric SrTiO<sub>3</sub>
items.summary: Cryo-STEM reveals that SrTiO3 forms periodic polar nanodomains below 105 K, but these fragment below 40 K, linking quantum paraelectricity to nanoscale polar ordering and disordering.

items.title: What counts as a moon? Huge ‘exosatellite’ sparks debate
items.summary: Discovery of a distant Jupiter-mass object could pave the way for detection of exomoons — plus, a rare transmissible cancer found in catfish.

items.title: Brown bullhead catfish melanoma represents a novel transmissible cancer
items.summary: Whole-genome sequencing analysis of tumour and matched non-tumour host tissues of the brown bullhead catfish reveals a type of naturally occurring transmissible cancer.

items.title: A radical approach to making C-glycoside molecules
items.summary: A platform for synthesizing highly desirable C-glycoside molecules from sugar has been developed that uses glycosyl sulfonyl hydrazides as readily accessible free-radical precursors. The strategy enables targeted formation of carbon–carbon bonds across carbohydrate scaffolds and with specificity for the desired 3D arrangement of atoms.

items.title: The planktonic microbiome of the Great Barrier Reef
items.summary: The Great Barrier Reef Microbial Genomes Database compiles prokaryotic, viral and eukaryotic genomes from seawater collected from the Great Barrier Reef, providing a rich resource for the study of marine microbial communities and ecosystem research and management.

items.title: Breathalyser can tell if you are burning fat from a single exhalation
items.summary: The compact device can measure when the body is in ketosis and could help people to manage weight loss.

items.title: How do quantum computers work?
items.summary: Recent breakthroughs suggest usable devices could be here in a decade.

items.title: Exceptional brain and ecological diversity in the earliest snakes
items.summary: A well-preserved fossil snake from the Late Cretaceous of Brazil shows early ecological and brain shape disparity in the group.

items.title: White House rolls out AI funding — and signals a new era for US science
items.summary: Chief US science adviser calls for a shakeup in funding while handing out grants to accelerate research with AI.

items.title: Briefing Chat: Baby T. rex were killers from birth, suggest new fossils
items.summary: Nature staff discuss the young but deadly dinosaur kings, the prowess of ancient Egyptian princesses, and how London is becoming the world’s AI safety capital.

items.title: Mapping drivers of life expectancy change in Asia from 1990 to 2023
items.summary: Using the Global Burden of Disease Study data across Asian countries and territories, life expectancy trends and the effects of cause-specific mortality and risk factors on changes in these trends are analysed.

items.title: Humanity spoke thousands of languages at the dawn of farming — now many of them are lost
items.summary: A shift from nomadic lifestyles could have triggered linguistic diversity before it then declined rapidly.

items.title: Air conditioning is not enough to keep people cool — can scientists find an alternative?
items.summary: Advances in materials allow buildings to be cooled as temperatures rise.

items.title: Could small-team science be dying out?
items.summary: The proportion of one- and two-author papers in the Nature Index is shrinking rapidly, as science done by big teams continues to surge.

items.title: Daily briefing: Orcas smash sunfish to smithereens
items.summary: The dolphins might be helping their young eat, or just having fun. Plus, the beauty and skill of scientific illustration and a crash course in quantum computing.

items.title: How does Make America Healthy Again hold up against scientific scrutiny?
items.summary: Researchers share their views on the US health policy spanning topics from vaccines to nutrition.

items.title: Rising stars of mathematics awarded prestigious 2026 Fields Medal
items.summary: Two of the four are the first Chinese-born winners of the prize since 1982.

items.title: Here’s what’s next for the Artemis II astronauts
items.summary: Newfound fame has proved to be stellar for some astronauts but harder for others. Will NASA’s popular crew need some space?

items.title: What The Odyssey reveals about ancient science — from botany to psychiatry
items.summary: From intelligent ships to clues about eclipses, Homer’s The Odyssey reveals how Bronze Age Greeks understood the world.

items.title: International PhD students to face strict limits on time in the US
items.summary: Trump administration takes action to address ‘forever students’.

items.title: ‘Good design takes mastery’: scientific illustrators sketch out AI’s future
items.summary: Nature talks to five artists about their approaches to communicating science visually.

items.title: Eyes upturned towards infinity
items.summary: Stars in our eyes.

items.title: How to use AI to make a graphical abstract in minutes
items.summary: Artificial intelligence is a democratizing force for those without graphic-design experience, as long as it is used conscientiously.

items.title: Three tips to avoid AI image mistakes in science
items.summary: Artificial-intelligence tools can be useful for brainstorming and creating graphics, but they can introduce errors. If you’re going to use them, here’s how to avoid problems.

items.title: Author Correction: Feature-specific threat coding in lateral septum guides defensive action
items.summary: Author Correction: Feature-specific threat coding in lateral septum guides defensive action
